source.title: Predicting Future Actions of Reinforcement Learning Agents
source.authors: Stephen Chung; S. Niekum; David Krueger

page_placements.theme: Explicit planning modules or planning tokens in RL and sequence agents

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether RL agents' internal states, including explicit plans, help predict future behavior in Sokoban, an additional task and architecture setting relative to the claim's language-model examples.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates supervised predictors of RL agents' future actions and events from agent inner states. It does not intervene on those states or test whether they causally change the agent's actions. The simulation-based results use separately trained world models rather than the agent's internal look-ahead, so they are not recorded as rows for V5. No language-model generation or rhyming-verse results are reported.
record.test_reason: The study decodes future actions and events from the hidden states of a DRC agent, an implicit planner in Sokoban, against a state-action baseline and a non-planning IMPALA control. That bears on V5 (internal look-ahead in Sokoban). MuZero and Thinker plan explicitly by construction (MCTS or world-model rollouts), so their results show designed planning, not emergent internal look-ahead. The simulation results use an external world model and are also not V5 evidence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the authors' point that DRC and IMPALA hidden states give only moderate action-prediction gains and no event-prediction gain. The authors explicitly leave open whether DRC gains reflect stored plans or an easier latent representation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains supervised predictors to use RL agents' plans or hidden states to predict future actions and events; it does not use language-model rhyme prompts or causal interventions on candidate future tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: The usefulness of auxiliary information differs by agent type and prediction target: hidden states modestly improve action prediction for DRC and IMPALA but do not improve their event prediction.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit planning agents' built-in rollouts (MuZero, Thinker) make future actions and events far more predictable. MuZero's 5-action accuracy rises from 40% to 87% with 50k training samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicitly constructed plans in model-based RL agents are faithful predictors of the agent's next several actions.

record.problems: The experiments cover only Sokoban and four RL algorithms. Predictors' ability to use internal information is measured, but the study does not intervene on plans to establish causal effects on agent behavior. Most Figure 2 results are not given as exact numbers in the text. The text describes Figure 2 error bars as standard deviations across three predictors, while the caption says two standard errors across 9 seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only per-training-data-size curves and the alternative-inner-state results in Appendix D were not transcribed as separate rows; the text does not provide their individual numerical values. Simulation-based predictor results and world-model ablations were left out because they use an external learned world model rather than the agent's internal look-ahead.

untested.parts: All: no language models or verse.
All: no test of whether features are computed for later positions.

Causal steering by internal plans (no interventions on DRC states). Chess, multi-step reasoning and other architectures. Horizons beyond 5 steps. Whether DRC hidden states encode plans rather than a convenient state representation (authors defer to interpretability).
Not tested for language models. The DRC results bear only loosely on whether apparent planning reduces to state features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label for MuZero and Thinker is dropped: their planning is designed, not emergent internal look-ahead. All DRC and IMPALA values are figure-only. The error-bar description conflicts between text (SD across 3 predictors) and caption (2 SE across 9 seeds). Appendix D reports DRC last tick vs all ticks as similar (figure-only), which is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model rhyme-word representations and causal interventions changing the intervening line.
Decodability of tokens several positions ahead from a language-model hidden state.
Whether language models compute features early for later positions rather than as a next-token side effect.
Rhyme planning in open-weight language models.
The study tests future-action and event predictability for RL agents in Sokoban, not multi-step reasoning or language generation; it does not causally test whether plans steer subsequent behavior.
Whether language-model planning is shallow, incidental, or causally ineffective.

relationships.condition: DRC (implicit planner) in Sokoban, supervised decoding of next 5 actions and of a 5-step event
relationships.reason: DRC hidden states give only a moderate action-prediction gain, no larger than non-planning IMPALA's (r3 vs r4), and no event-prediction gain (r7). The authors cannot attribute the gain to plans, so this decoding gives no evidence for look-ahead beyond a state representation.
relationships.display_finding: Hidden states gave only moderate gains in predicting five future actions, no greater than non-planning IMPALA, and no gain for five-step events, leaving those gains unattributable to plans.

relation.reason: The study experimentally compares future-action and event prediction with and without agent inner states, bearing on internal look-ahead beyond verse.

tranche.reason: The Sokoban experiments provide results relevant to V5 in an RL setting, including an implicit planner and a non-planning control.

source_check.notes: Appendix A explicitly identifies DRC(3,3). Uncertainty reporting is inconsistent: Section 5.1 describes standard deviations across three predictors, whereas Figure 2 specifies two standard errors across nine seeds.

statements.correction: Section 5.1: DRC and IMPALA both show moderate action-prediction improvements; neither shows an event-prediction improvement. Stored plans and easier-to-learn latent representations remain alternative explanations. No numerical or statistical ordering of their gains is stated.
statements.problem: The text describes both DRC and IMPALA gains as moderate; it does not establish that DRC's gain is no larger. The authors leave plan attribution unresolved.

statements.correction: Section 5.1: both agents show moderate action-prediction gains; neither improves event prediction; plan attribution remains unresolved. Appendix A: DRC(3,3), trained for 25 million transitions. Predictor training sizes: 1k, 2k, 5k, 10k, 20k, 50k.
statements.problem: The asserted ordering of DRC and IMPALA gains is stronger than the text supports. Although omitted from the pack's subject description, the DRC configuration is specified in the paper.

statements.correction: Tested agents: MuZero, Thinker, DRC(3,3), and IMPALA without its LSTM component. IMPALA has convolutional residual blocks and is included in the hidden-state prediction comparison. Transformer and language-model agents are not tested.
statements.problem: The claim that Sokoban architectures outside DRC are untested is too broad: this paper also tests IMPALA and two explicit planners.

statements.correction: Section 5.1: both DRC and IMPALA gain moderately on action prediction and gain nothing on the selected event. Distinguishing stored plans from easier latent representations requires further interpretation of the internal circuits.
statements.problem: The paper leaves plan-specific information unresolved; it does not establish that DRC has no plan-specific predictive gain over IMPALA.

statements.correction: DRC action decoding improves moderately; IMPALA also improves moderately. DRC event decoding does not improve. Whether the action-decoding gain reflects plans is unresolved.
statements.problem: The description of this study as finding no plan-specific gain should distinguish an unresolved attribution from a demonstrated absence.

statements.correction: Appendix A: DRC(3,3), trained for 25 million transitions. Section 5.1: moderate action-prediction gains for both DRC and IMPALA; no event-prediction gains; plan attribution unresolved. MuZero all-five-action accuracy: 40% baseline, 87% with plans, using 50k training examples.
statements.problem: The paper does not establish that DRC's gain is no greater than IMPALA's. Its Appendix A resolves the stated uncertainty about the DRC configuration.
